utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have -- if we could go into private session for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, at some point after the 16th of July and the incidents at Pilica, did Lieutenant Colonel Popovic actually tell you what units were able to assist him in the operation around Pilica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. About how many days after the 16th did he tell you this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About five to six days after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told me that during the operation in which he was personally present, that he was assisted by the units of the Main Staff, that is, Pelemis's unit and units from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, any cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Good afternoon. I think we're not in private session any longer, are we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First I would like to pose some very direct questions with respect to Colonel Blagojevic of the Bratunac Brigade. It's my understanding from reading all of your statements and listening to your testimony, it is your belief and understanding that at no time did Colonel Blagojevic, to your knowledge, send any men, either to Orahovac, Branjevo Military Farm, or Pilica, to participate in any of the killing operations of which you were participating in, either directly or indirectly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as Orahovac and Branjevo are concerned, I don't have any information that people from that particular unit had been sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what about Pilica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area of Pilica is part of Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And as we know now, after Popovic was through executing the prisoners in Branjevo Farm, later on that afternoon on -- I believe it was July 16th, 1995, he then went to Pilica where he proceeded to execute the remainder batch of prisoners that he had there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we do know, we do know with some certainty that members from the Bratunac Brigade were sent to assist the Zvornik Brigade on July 15th and on July 16th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's my understanding, and correct me if I'm wrong, that the soldiers that came from the Bratunac Brigade came in two different shifts, were on two different times. And on both times they came in order to assist the very heavy fighting that was going on in the area of Batkovice [sic]. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area of Baljkovice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. And that is where the Zvornik Brigade, as I understand, under the command of -- of acting command Obrenovic, and later on with -- when Pandurevic came when the Zvornik Brigade was actually taking some very heavy losses from the Muslim fighters as they were trying to make their way to Tuzla. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact yesterday you indicated that on one of the intercepts where there is the description of the situation was horrible, the reference you indicated was to the situation on the front line where the Zvornik Brigade was taking very heavy losses from the Muslim fighters, who had been on the run for several days and were trying to fight their way to Tuzla. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This referred to Baljkovice where Muslim forces had suffered severe losses and chaos reigned in the area, which was also indicated in the report of Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Correct. And yesterday you were able to assist with the interpretation of one particular intercept, an intercept that has been played here with some regularity and with some prominence, I might add, and I'm referring to Exhibit P257/A. In that particular intercept, sir, you were asked to give your opinion with respect to what was being said as to whether some men had arrived from Colonel Blagojevic. Do you recall being asked that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If I could just briefly correct the record. The intercept has not been played. I think that was just a mischoice of words. I don't want to leave the impression that there is an audio intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I indicated that it played a prominence in this courtroom, not that it was played in the courtroom. But it has been -- and thank you, Madam Usher, for assisting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That particular intercept that I was referring to, and again it has marked for identification purposes as P257/A, that was the intercept that was shown to you, sir, was it not, with respect to references being made by Lieutenant Colonel Popovic with respect to men arriving from Blagojevic. Do you recall that particular intercept, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I believe you've testified yesterday, as you have told the Prosecutor in the past, that that intercept is -- the inquiry that is being made by Popovic or by the person inquiring of Popovic was with respect to reinforcements that were supposed to arrive from the Bratunac Brigade and deployed to Baljkovice. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, prior to coming here yesterday, and in fact prior to Sunday, in all your various encounters with the Office of the Prosecution you never indicated that on the morning of the 16th at approximately - and the time varies - (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: nowhere prior to Sunday, sir, and yesterday, sir, have you ever indicated that Lieutenant Colonel Popovic asked you to contact the Bratunac Brigade for reinforcements for any killing operation. Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stated this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact the first time that you stated it was Sunday in the afternoon, while you were being briefed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At that point while you were being briefed, since it was not a tape recorded briefing, and given the importance and the uniqueness of the information that you were providing at that time, the Office of the Prosecution requested that you give a statement with respect to that particular information. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I gave that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That was on Sunday that you gave it, January 25th, 2004. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it was during that time for the first time that you mentioned anything about being asked by Popovic to contact the Bratunac Brigade in order to get assistance for the killing operation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, in fact, during that conversation that you had on Sunday, that was the 25th of January, 2004, you also indicated that later on in the day there was a second communication with the Bratunac Brigade, that one being to see whether the reinforcements for the Baljkovice assistance was on its way. Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on Sunday when you brought this matter up, that is two days ago on the 25th of January, 2004, you indicated that when you contacted the Bratunac Brigade, you informed them that it was for the purpose of this killing operation that was going on. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please, I'm afraid I have not understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me go a little slower then, sir. When you met with them on -- when you met with the Prosecutor on the 25th of January, 2004, you indicated that when you placed that phone call to Badem, that is the Bratunac Brigade command post in Bratunac, and you spoke with the duty officer, that you informed him of the purpose, that is, that you told him that it was for the purpose of assisting Popovic in the killing operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This conversation took place in the morning with the duty officer, and it concerned the assistance to be provided to Popovic for the purposes of the execution operation in the area of Pilica and Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then yesterday you indicated some additional information, again rather new, when you were asked the question whether you put it in some coded terms, and the answer to that question was yes. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, but still I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. My question, sir, is: Yesterday for the very first time you indicated that this time when you called the Bratunac Brigade, you had told them in an indirect manner, as opposed to a direct manner, whether they could provide assistance for what was going on with respect to Popovic's mission, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The request was addressed to them directly by telephone, and they were also told why it was necessary for this assistance to be provided, for those men to be sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you indicated yesterday for the first time that you put it in coded words or coded terms, as opposed to telling them directly on a line: "We need you. We need some men in order to kill some Muslims in Branjevo Farm or in Pilica." Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing coded could have been conveyed by telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Maybe it's my -- I apologise for not being clear. I'm not suggesting that you were sending a coded message, but you were speaking in a way that was an indirect way, a coded way, so that you could alarm them of the true nature of the request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I said that, but once again I did not fully understand your previous question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not referring to your question. I was actually referring to the question that had been put to me by the Prosecutor yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Was there any reason why, assuming that this conversation took place, was there any reason why you did not mention this earlier to the Prosecutor, that is, that you had this conversation with the duty officer of the Bratunac Brigade on the morning of the 16th -- July 16th, 1995. What was the reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This information concerns myself and my direct involvement in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I understand that. But my question is: Why, sir, have you waited until the night before you're about to testify to claim that you had this conversation? Why not raise it days, weeks, or months earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had decided to tell the whole truth, the whole truth about an incident in which I had personally participated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's talk about how you got to be -- how you got to that position, that is, the position where you wanted to tell the whole truth. Initially, you had been contacted by the Office of the Prosecution on August 14th, 2002. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At that time you were in the United States and you were being interviewed by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, otherwise known as the FBI. True?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you had a meeting on the -- August 18th, a few days later, where the Prosecutor requested whether you would be willing to give them an interview, and you indicated that you would. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I believe it was at that meeting sometime around -- where you met on the 19th and 20th of August, 2002, and at that point in time you had, in fact, indicated to the Office of the Prosecution that you were

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Subsequent to that, there was a telephone conversation. I believe it was November 15th, 2002, where again the Prosecution expressed their desire to meet and to get a statement from you. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then in March 30th, 2003, you were approached, and you -- and the Office of the Prosecution suggested, or inquired I should say, that would be the better term, inquired whether you wished to consider being a witness in the witness protection programme. Correct? Is that correct? That was back on March 30th, 2003.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it at that point in time they explained to you to some detail, perhaps not in the greatest of detail but in some detail, what it all entailed, that is, being in the witness protection programme, you and your family. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the following day, on March 31st, 2003, you were arrested by the FBI, given that you had provided false information in order to obtain a visa to live, you and your family, in the United States. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at some point, as I know the procedure and I see from the documents, you were presented or you were offered a federal public defender, someone to represent you, for free, correct, free of charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I did pay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All those were court costs; I understand that. But it was explained to you at that point -- the charges were explained to you, and at some point you entered a plea of guilty to two of the counts on the indictment. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were not given a sentence, but instead according to the judgement that we have, you were remanded to the custody of the Immigration and Naturalisation Office in the United States, pending your deportation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So, in other words, when Mr. McCloskey asked you yesterday whether you had spent any time in gaol, in fact you were there in detention waiting to be deported, as opposed to serving a sentence resulting from your change of plea to guilty on two charges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not in detention; I was in a prison facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. All right. We can -- you were in a prison facility not serving a sentence but waiting when you and your family would be deported from the United States back to Bosnia and Herzegovina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the trial, I was handed over to the immigration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Okay. And it was right upon that point in time, in fact the date -- the day that you pled guilty, that you met a representative from the Office of the Prosecution, Ms. Davis, and it was that day or the following day, on July 10th, 2003, that you began some other discussions with respect to the witness protection programme. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Ms. Davis of the Office of the Prosecution was very clear in expressing to you that no immunity would be provided to you, immunity from being prosecuted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm not sure what counsel is referring to, but Ms. Anne Davis of the Office of the Prosecutor had no involvement in this as far as I can recall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe there's another Davis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There could be. But I'm referring to their information reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There may have been a lawyer named that, but I'm -- perhaps someone from the witness protection programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may for one second, Your Honour, I might be able to assist. Davis is a common name; I'll concede to that point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My lawyer, whose name is David, spoke to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, if that's so -- well, in any event, it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were explained -- in any event, you were explained that you were not being provided with immunity, but if you continued to cooperate with the OTP, the OTP would look after you and your family. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A promise was made that myself and my family would be taken care of, but I never received any promise related in any way to my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Correct. But the caveat, the -- I'm trying to find the right word to make sure that we understand each other. The responsibility was placed on your shoulders that you would be truthful in your cooperation with the Office of the Prosecution. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In other words, they were only willing to assist you to the extent that you were willing to be truthful and honest with respect to your involvement and your knowledge regarding the events in Orahovac, Branjevo Farm, Pilica, and any other matters that you may -- you had knowledge of regarding the Srebrenica incidents. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wanted to help me in general terms.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure whether she understood the answer correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say they wanted to help you in general terms, well they wanted you to help them; and in return, they would help you. It was a two-way street. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't have to help them in any way. I had already given them my statement in America, with certain amendments, certain things that I had left out at that time. And I have already explained why I did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But at this point in time, we haven't left the United States. We're still back on July 10th, between July 10th and July 24th, 2003, when you are waiting to see whether you and your family would be accepted into the witness protection programme. And so I want to make clear that I understand the situation as it were back then. You understood that in return for your truthfulness, they were going to try to secure witness protection status for you and your family. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wanted to help me because of the cooperation that I had provided them until that time. And I also personally expressed my willingness to continue the same cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And on July 24th, 2003, you were indeed informed by representatives of the Office of the Prosecution, or the witness protection programme that's provided by the Tribunal, that you and your family had been accepted into the witness protection programme. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that -- and later on, I believe it was October 27, 2003, you were informed that you would be deported back to Bosnia and Herzegovina before you could be relocated to a third country, correct, you and your family? Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, during this period of time you were assisting the Office of the Prosecution, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know which period you're referring to. Could you please specify.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, up until let's say the end of October 2003, you had been assisting them, giving them information. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And after that period, on November 10th, 2003, you were shown some documents by the Office of the Prosecution, including the green-coloured notebook. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the reason for giving you this green-coloured notebook was to see whether you could recognise your handwriting and whether you could assist the Office of the Prosecution in interpreting some of the notes that were in that notebook. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reason was for me to identify the book and to remind myself of my personal participation in all those events that were noted down in that book, which was used as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, before being shown this book, you were not aware that the Office of the Prosecution had this book, had this piece of evidence in their possession. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, in fact, because you did not know that they had this information in their possession with -- which in part implicated you specifically, you were giving false versions or false information to the Prosecution with respect to your participation in the events of the 14th, 15th, 16th of July, 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Prior to being shown this notebook on November 10th, 2003, you were not aware that the Prosecutor had this notebook in his -- in its possession. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before November -- what date?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: November 10, 2003.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And prior to this date, you had given the Prosecution certain versions of your participation of the events. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what versions you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to false versions, as opposed to truthful versions. Does that help your recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, now that your recollection has been refreshed, would you agree with me that prior to seeing that notebook, you had been giving false information to the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No -- partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for correcting me. I'm not suggesting that you were -- your entire version or entire story was false, but nonetheless you would agree with me that with respect to your involvement, one, there was false information. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And also, aside from false information, there was information that you withheld?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, once you saw that notebook, I would suspect that upon seeing your own handwriting and having your memory refreshed, you would have been armed and prepared to give the Office of the Prosecution a truthful and honest and complete account of your involvement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. One of the reasons the Prosecutor gave you that book was to refresh your memory. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Because you had indicated that you needed, you know, certain facts you couldn't recall. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Upon opening that notebook, you recognised your own handwriting. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you also recognised that this notebook placed you right in the centre of the events of July 16, 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not only the book itself, but in fact my personal involvement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But I'm talking about the book itself. Once the Prosecutor showed it to you and once you read your handwriting and once you saw your notations, there was no escaping your past. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Incidentally, if we were to go into this notebook and check on July 16, 1995, and check your handwriting when you were the duty officer, is it not a fact, sir, that we would not find any notations made by you that you had been instructed by Colonel Popovic, Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, to contact Badem, the Bratunac Brigade, in order to request assistance. We wouldn't find any notations, would we?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But we do find, we do find - and I underscore that - notes that certainly are incriminating to you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, on December 3rd, 2003, you met with the Office of the Prosecution, and if memory serves me correct, Mr. McCloskey, the Prosecutor, was there. And in case you don't recall what occurred on that day, that is the date when Mr. McCloskey expressed some disappointment in you and indicated that he believed that you had not been telling the truth. Do you recall that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, in fact, to his credit, Mr. McCloskey suggested -- in fact, he indicated that he would be contacting the Registrar to ensure that you would have a lawyer representing you in order to protect your rights. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we could stop right here for one second and focus on what is happening at the family front, your family front. This is the same period of time, is it not, sir, when the Office of the Prosecution, through its efforts with the Tribunal, have arranged for you and your family to be in the witness protection programme. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You have already been told that arrangements will be made for you and your family to go to a third country. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in spite of that good will on the part of the Office of the Prosecution, in spite of them having met their part of the bargain, you were continuing to provide them with either false and/or incomplete information. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you indicate -- yesterday you indicated that you are not getting anything out of this arrangement that you have the Office of the Prosecution. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In other words, they have not promised that they will not indict you, as they should?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not promise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But your family is, in fact, getting a benefit, are they not, by being relocated to a third country. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And should you get indicted and should you be sentenced to a prison term, would being in the witness protection programme provide assistance to your family during the period that you are serving your sentence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if we look at it in those terms, you are, in fact, getting some sort of benefit, or at least your family is. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, after that encounter with Mr. McCloskey on December 3, 2003, you gave another -- you had an opportunity to meet with a very fine lawyer, if I may say so, a very experienced lawyer, at least with respect to this particular Tribunal, Mr. O'Sullivan. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it Mr. O'Sullivan was able to answer all of your questions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, was he able to answer all of your legal questions; in other words, solve any legal dilemmas you might have with respect to your status?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: These are general questions related to legal consultations with one's lawyer is sacred ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think the communication between him and his counsel should be in secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am not suggesting that it shouldn't be, Your Honour. I'm not delving into it. And as a Defence lawyer, I know that the sanctity of the ground that I'm stepping on. But I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's very difficult for this person to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take the Prosecutor's objection and it's well-founded, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At some point on January 21, 2004, you agreed to meet with the Office of the Prosecution. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that was a, that was a -- you were not compelled at that point, as with in any other time, past or future, you were not compelled to meet with the Office of the Prosecution. You were not forced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. In other words, you were doing that voluntarily. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pursuant to the request, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But each and every time the Office of the Prosecution - at least what I've been able to glean from the documents - were very careful to make sure that you understood your fundamental rights, one being the right to remain silent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And on January 21st, you gave another interview. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, in fact, from what I understand from the Prosecution, that was the interview where apparently part of the tape was not functioning, one of the sides of the tape apparently wasn't functioning. So we only have one portion of that interview. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so by this point in time, January 21st, 2004, which is only last week, this is the very first time when apparently you are willing to tell the Office of the Prosecution your entire involvement in this affair. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For instance, we know by now, as a result of that particular interview, that on the -- after -- on the 14th, 13th and 14th of July, 1995, you were one of the main organisers of the executions that took place in Orahovac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean? Could you please repeat the question. What do you mean when you say "the main organiser"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Not that you were one. You were one of the main organisers, not the main. At the top we have Beara, then Popovic, then Nikolic, but you were the detail person on the ground, were you not, to organise the orderly process of the executions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. I think there are people above Mr. Beara, so that's a misstatement of the evidence, regarding the organising of this. I think the facts are pretty clear that Mr. Mladic had a role in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be heard for a second, and I think I have been very clear with respect to General Mladic's involvement. But this gentleman here has never mentioned Mladic, so I don't want to go that far. I'm not denying that, but he's indicated that Nikolic at one point told him -- or he's indicated that Beara was instructing Nikolic, words to that effect. We know that Popovic was on the ground. So that's why the omission. So with that qualification, and I accept Mr. McCloskey's assertion that General Mladic was involved and is perhaps responsible for these events. With that qualification, I want to make sure that we're clear on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe the phrase "organiser" is not a proper one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You know, Mladic is in the high, top position, but the witness himself, I don't think --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At one point in time, sir, on the 14th and 15th, were you not asked to -- well, organise the orderly process of execution. Correct? You along with Jasikovac, the chief of police.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I believe it was the chief of police that had requested assistance in cutting the ribbons in order to blindfold the prisoners. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The commander of the military police. Thank you for correcting me. And you -- your -- one of your functions was to organise the people, the prisoners, so they could get loaded onto the buses and so that the executions could take place in an orderly and expeditious fashion. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To organise the VRS members, to take the men out of the gym, and to put them onto motor vehicles, and to dispatch the vehicles to the execution sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Correct. And, in fact, it was because of your organisational skills and experience in this process that Popovic, on the 16th, requested that you go to Branjevo Farm to assist there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But on that day, you were the designated duty officer, and so that is why Drago Nikolic insisted that you remain behind. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, were you not the duty officer that day, the designated duty officer that day, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. I believe that's a contradictory two-part question. I think there's a difference between the duty officer of that day and the designated duty officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will go about it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a very important distinction, Your Honour. They had a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's what I'm trying to get at, Your Honour. And as I understand from reading the testimony of his previous statements, he's indicated that he was on the list for that day. That's what -- I'm trying to get that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's fine. I have no objection to that simple question. It's the two-part question that is problematic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could split your question one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps we could -- not to nail this point to take our -- I guess I can keep going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We have 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were designated -- it was your turn on that day to be the duty officer. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you were not on the list to be the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. In other words, the acting commander at the time would have made that decision. Since Pandurevic was gone, that would have been Obrenovic or his designated representative who had made that decision as to who would fill in and serve out that day as duty officer. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or the senior duty operations officer who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And that's why -- that's one of the reasons why Drago Nikolic couldn't accommodate Popovic, because it was not up to him, that is, Drago Nikolic, to excuse you from your functions as a duty officer for that particular day. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drago did not relieve me of my duty on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He could not relieve you; that's my whole point. It was not within his powers to relieve you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so when you had that exchange with Mr. McCloskey yesterday whether Drago Nikolic was giving an order to Popa, as you put it, Popovic, it wasn't that he was giving him an order that you could not go, it's just that he was explaining the situation that you had to be left behind as the duty officer. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I had to stay to take care of the obligations that I have at the security branch, that was the first thought that I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. All right. We won't -- we'll get into this in another way. Now, on -- when you first met with the Prosecutor, you never told them about your involvement at all on the 14th and 15th, that is, that you stayed behind and that you assisted in the executions, did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's a misstatement of the evidence. I -- it can be done, I think, clearer and it will make sense. He did tell us about the 14th. Partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's my whole point. Half a truth is half a lie, Your Honour. That's what I'm trying to get at. I'll go about it another way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll go about it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you first met with the Office of the Prosecution, you told them that at some point when the executions were about to begin or had just begun, you left on the 14th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I said after the executions, after three vehicles had passed I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And you told them -- in fact, you told them that the reason you wanted to leave and the reason that you were asked to leave was because you didn't want to be there, that was one reason; and the second reason was that your family, in the midst of all this madness and Zvornik being attacked and everything, was on its way for a vacation at the seaside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, sir, during those executions, you never once expressed an unwillingness, an unwillingness, to participate in them, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, on the morning of the 16th, as I recall, you wake up sometime around 6.00 o'clock, or perhaps even earlier, 5.30. Correct? This is while you are in Zvornik at the command post.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you indicate there -- you've indicated to the Prosecution that at some time after that, that you see Popovic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drago and Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. It's my understanding that you're designated the duty officer, and it's after that that you claim for the first time on the 25th of January that Popovic asked you to contact the Bratunac Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, getting back to where we started, when I asked you: Why did you wait until the evening or the afternoon of January 25th, 2004, the night before you're supposed to testify, how is it that you waited that long to say, Oh, yes, by the way, I was asked to have this conversation -- to have this contact with the Bratunac Brigade, how is it that you waited that long, and why is it that you didn't bring it up on January 21st, when you did, in fact, incriminate yourself by placing yourself right in the executions on the 14th and 15th as well as your participation in the 16th and thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Based on the discussions regarding the participation of the units and the executions in the area of Pilica and Rocevic on that day, that is, which particular units had taken part in it and where the request for assistance for carrying out this particular assignment was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So if I understand -- I'm going to try and see if I can interpret your answer. Are you suggesting, sir, that with all your conversations with the Prosecution and them showing you documents, it triggered some thought, some memory, that was dormant, hidden in your memory cells, and as a result that's why on Sunday, the night before you testified, you realise that these -- that you had been instructed to make these calls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had not been instructed. My memory was refreshed and concerning the request and -- of -- and the participation of the units which were present, and also the units that took part but whom I didn't know were present. That's how I got this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, with respect to the refreshing of your memory, we know, do we not, that once when your memory was refreshed on November 10th, 2003, you proceeded to provide false information to the Prosecutor. Correct? We've established that, have we not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: November what -- the 10th? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So when the Prosecutor was attempting to refresh your memory and assist you with documents, you provided false and incorrect information nonetheless. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you met -- then you met with your lawyer and you gave an interview, and I would suspect, given that you had more time to consider your predicament, more time to think of the family, which obviously you want to protect, you gave an interview on January 21st with a refreshed memory. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's -- at that point in time is when you tell us that you were a participant. But how is it that with that refreshed memory on January 21st, you omit stating that Popovic instructed you to contact the Bratunac Brigade on the 16th of July, and that you had this alleged conversation where you told them: "We need men for the killing operation." How is it that you could forget such a thing with this refreshed memory?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The question can be "omit" or "forget", but the two are contradictory. So choose one, but you can't ask him the same contradictory question; it's impossible to answer. I have no problem with either question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But the main idea is there, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How is it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We need a clear question for the witness to be able to answer. How is it, sir? This is not a clear question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I thought I won the objection, maybe I was wrong, and I was relying -- so if the objection was sustained, I just went and I just -- that was sort of a booster to the witness. If the objection was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If the objection was overruled, if the objection was sustained, I'll rephrase the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, I have no problem with your question, Mr. Karnavas. But in order for the witness to understand you better, you may split the question or choose one to ask your question, just to facilitate. And after this question is answered, we'll have the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How is it, sir, that after having your memory refreshed, you omitted to state to the Prosecutor on tape that Popovic on the morning of the 16th had instructed you to contact the Bratunac Brigade and to ask for assistance for the killing operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already stated that the conversation was about the participation of the units in this operation and which particular units took part. The units that were requested to take part in the operation on that day, it's impossible for someone to say everything. My memory was being refreshed as we talked about the events that had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just one last - not a question to answer now - but a thought where we'll pick up. Maybe during the break you can think of what documents in particular refreshed your memory with respect to this particular conversation. Because thus far, I dare say, at least in my disclosure material, I have no documents that would verify that you had this conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object to -- first of all, this is an argumentative comment designed to challenge the witness's credibility to be left on a break. That's no sense -- it doesn't get us anywhere, that he be argumentative like this. And it should be -- it's unnecessary. And to leave a witness on the break with this kind of air is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I see no problem for this kind of practice. I think the witness will answer if there's any documents or not. If not, it's all right. Whatever the answer is, we'll take it. There's no problem about that. Well, I think it's time for a break, and we'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, before you start, I think I have to remind you that this witness is a protected witness. So when you ask some questions, especially of some specific positions and locations, please be careful. Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, prior to the break, I asked you if you could provide us with any specific documents that you might have referred to refresh your recollection that would -- that helped you come up with this information, that is, that on the morning of the 16th of July, 1995, you did in fact contact the Bratunac Brigade, spoke with the duty officer, and left a message requesting for assistance for the killing operations. Could you please tell us what specific documents you used to refresh your recollection.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't have any specific documents in connection with this issue; however, based on the deployment of the units which took part in the operation and based on the contacts that I had with Popovic concerning the overall operation and also on the basis of the assistance which had to be sent, either to Baljkovice and Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, it is a fact, is it not, that Lieutenant Colonel Popovic never indicated to you that members of the Bratunac Brigade had participated in any of the executions that were taking place in Pilica or in Branjevo Farm on July 16th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. He did, however, mention, did he not, certain units that he believed were the participants and were assisting him in that killing operation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that unit was the, I believe, the 10th Sabotage Detachment from Bijeljina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, I don't know where exactly they were from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But you do know that they are attached to or part of the Main Staff. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I believe I've seen somewhere where it was brought to your attention about the Panteri unit. Did Mr. -- did Lieutenant Colonel Popovic ever mention them at all, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not under the name of Panteri.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you, sir, at any point in time make any reference or invoke, I should say, the name of Colonel Blagojevic while you were being proofed on Sunday, January 25, 2004?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The unit from Bratunac, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But did you actually state -- did you actually use his name? That's what my question is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But you never had any contact with Colonel Blagojevic, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You never spoke to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean in connection with the task of the 15th and the 16th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. In fact, you never spoke to him with respect to any tasks that you were involved with respect to killing Muslim prisoners. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we could go back to the 14th and sort of try to cover some points over there, on that date. As I understand it from your testimony, sometime on July 14th you were asked to go to Bratunac to meet with Momir Nikolic in order to turn over some humanitarian aid. I believe that -- I apologise, that was the 13th. 13th of July. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to turn over the convoy to the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now, that convoy was a Russian convoy, was it not, of humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I believe the battalion commander, the Russian battalion commander, was there along with you in that convoy. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was there any particular reason why they said: "Go and meet Momir Nikolic," if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not said that I should go and meet with Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Was it said that you should just go to the Bratunac Brigade? I mean ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to the security branch to turn over the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so that's why when you got to Bratunac and you went to the headquarters, you sought out Momir Nikolic, who was the head of security and intelligence for the Bratunac Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You indicated when you got there you learned that he wasn't there, and so you went off to Potocari, which is only approximately five kilometres away. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And there you saw Momir Nikolic with whom you were acquainted, you knew of him, you knew what he looked like. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As I understand your testimony and -- from yesterday and from before, you saw him walking around, and I believe yesterday you said that he was talking at some point. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at that point you informed him that you had this humanitarian convoy with you, and you asked him what to do with it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't inform him of that at that moment, while he was talking. I informed him on the occasion of our first encounter, as soon as I entered Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. That's what I'm talking about. As soon as you met him in Potocari, you spoke with him, and in fact as I recall, you asked him what was going on, who were these people that were there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You believed because of the lighting conditions, the setting of the sun, and the terrain that it would have been between 4.00 and 5.00 o'clock in the afternoon. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the timing may be important for other reasons. Was it closer to 5.00? Was it after 5.00? Was it closer to 4.00? Which of it is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's difficult to tell the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. In any event, when you did meet with him, he did not accept the humanitarian aid, but rather directed you back to Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not Momir Nikolic who directed me back to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did he accept the humanitarian aid, yes or no, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The humanitarian aid was accepted in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Just so that I make sure that I'm clear, before you met with Momir Nikolic, did you drop off the humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You went to Potocari. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You met with Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then you went back to Bratunac with the Russian commander, battalion commander. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's when you believe you went to the -- what you were told to be the mayor's office. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it was at that time that you believe the humanitarian aid was unloaded from the convoy. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not that I believed that. We were working on the organisation of the unloading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you physically watched the convoy being unloaded? Is that a yes or a no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Hence why I said "believe." Now, as I understand it you were there for approximately two hours or so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And were you meeting with a military man or a civilian when you were at what you believed to be the mayor's office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it, as customary as it is, you, the commander of the Russian Battalion, and the mayor probably sat around, had a discussion, perhaps have a few drinks while you were waiting for the convoy to be unloaded. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't even wait for the convoy to be unloaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But my question was: You were waiting there for two hours, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you were in the mayor's office with the Russian commander, battalion commander, did you have the ceremonial rakija that is normally served as part of the hospitality in that part of the world?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember as far as they were concerned, but I myself do not drink alcohol.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And at some point in time, you left and you went back to the Zvornik Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you got there, Drago Nikolic approached you requesting to know where had you been, because you had the official vehicle that is designated to the security of the Zvornik Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it was at that time when Drago Nikolic told you that you had to go to Orahovac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At that point in time, did he tell you that you were being sent off on a murder operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you think or suspect that you would be going to a murder operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to make sure that I understand this. Today your testimony is: Even before you left Zvornik and even though Drago Nikolic did not tell you anything about killing innocent, unarmed, Muslims, you believed that he was sending you to murder them. Correct? Is that your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me go about it in another way. When you gave your deposition in the United States, you had indicated that you thought that the men, the Muslim men, would be executed once you got there and you saw that they were getting off the bus and throwing off -- throwing out everything that they had from their pockets and their hats and what have you, that it was at that point in time that you realise that they were going to be executed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall making that statement in the United States during the deposition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record, less there be any misunderstanding, I'm reading from page 34 and I've just read from lines -- paraphrased from lines 10 to 13. And this would be marked for identification purposes as D109/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you indicated a slightly different variation, that when you arrived and you saw the Muslims coming off the bus, you immediately knew that they were going to be executed. Do you recall stating that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Today you're telling us that even before leaving Zvornik, you suspected that you were being sent off to where innocent Muslim prisoners were going to be executed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what I assumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you assumed even before you left Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assumed that after I left Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, was it on the road as you left Zvornik town and driving along the Drina River that you came with this -- that you had this suspicion or was it when you got there and first saw them or was it when you saw them being asked to empty their pockets and take their hats off? Which of the three versions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The departure to Orahovac and the arrival and the accommodation of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Incidentally, sir, had you participated, you personally participated in execution of innocent -- well, in Muslim prisoners of war prior to this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you got there and you realised that you had -- well, you had the suspicion that they were going to be executed, surely you must have voiced some objection to this monstrous deed that you suspected was about to occur.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that directly to anyone. I just thought it to myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it was sometime later when Drago Nikolic came and Popovic came when you learned explicitly from Nikolic that these innocent people that were sitting there unarmed were going to be executed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May I ask you, during that period of time how many hours had passed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In which period?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From the moment that you arrived in Orahovac until the moment where Nikolic and Popovic arrive and you learn that they're going to be executed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 13th in the evening until the early evening hours of the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So we're talking nearly 20 hours or 24 hours, 20 hours that you're there, give or take an hour or two. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And during this 20-hour period, you had this suspicion. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May I ask: What was going through your mind during that 20-hour period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, how on earth can I remember that now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you stop at least for one second, not an hour, not a minute, but one second to think and realise that this was senseless and inhumane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Having spent that second, did you then spend another second at least thinking that perhaps you should contact your commanding officer, either Pandurevic, who was in the field, or Obrenovic, who was there back in Zvornik as the acting commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You did, however, contact, as I understand, the duty officer on the 14th when you suspected that there were -- that this was a security -- a security risk to you, to Jasikovac, and to the military police over there, and that perhaps due to the large number of prisoners that were waiting their execution, that you needed more man power for security. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you contacted the duty officer, at least from what I have read thus far and what I heard yesterday, there is no mention at all that at any point in time you informed the duty officer of what your suspicions were at the time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The duty officer was notified. In fact, the duty operations officer was notified that there were some personnel needs and what needed to be done in order to send the personnel in to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The personnel needs that were, as you put it, were for the security, to assist in securing these prisoners of war. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To reinforce the security detail, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: To reinforce the security detail that was there securing prisoners of war. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. For the security of the prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you did not state anywhere in the past or yesterday that you indicated to the security officer [sic] that what you really needed them -- let me rephrase. That the -- that subsequent to the security, subsequent to securing these prisoners, that they would be executed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say that they would be executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, in fact, when you contacted the duty officer, that was prior, before, you had been told by Momir -- by Drago Nikolic that they would be executed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You did, however --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but I have just realised that in line 18 of the transcript the term "security officer" in fact should have -- it should read the duty officer who was not notified of that, because this is quite clear from the next question. The witness did not inform the duty officer, and not the security officer, as is stated here in line 18. So we are not talking about the security officer, but the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think this is a question put forward by Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with Mr. Stojanovic. I must have misspoken. This whole line of questioning deals with his communications with the duty officer at the time. So I'll rephrase it, Your Honour, and re-ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, do we have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think he cleared it up in the question, I don't -- otherwise I would object to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, as I understand, you did call someone else, aside from the duty officer, did you not, Lazar Ristic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But that was not the duty officer, but the duty operations officer of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As I understand, he was the deputy commander of the -- what is it? The 4th Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you indicated that he was nearby and that is the reason why you reached out to him for assistance. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Had he been a prior colleague of yours in the security organ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the security organ of the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you didn't contact his superior, you contacted him, I take it, because of his association with or experience in the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's a misstatement of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Which evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Had he been a colleague of yours in the security organ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before that. In the security organ of the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, when -- and as I understand it, at some point some reinforcements did come as a result of your request. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe you mentioned the two individuals yesterday when you testified -- among those that came, two individuals that you knew. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when they came, was it your impression that they knew that there -- that they were there to assist in any killing operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when -- at some point, as you indicated, that Drago Nikolic came and you had informed him that there had been an incident with respect to a couple of prisoners that had been shot and killed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's when he told you more or less, "Don't worry about that. They're all going to be killed," or words to that effect. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was said, "What problems? All of them will be executed immediately."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. At that point in time when he told you this, you did not express any reservation about executing them, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, in fact, after that you proceeded to assist him and Popovic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we know or we have learned that Drago Nikolic, who as I understand is a nasty piece of work, actually personally got involved in killing prisoners. Is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not there, up there, in that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you, sir, kill anyone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe you asked this question already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That was before that incident, Your Honour, whether he had killed anybody prior to the -- to this incident, because he indicated today in his testimony, Your Honour, that as he was setting off from Zvornik, he understood that this was going to be a murder operation, which led me to think that perhaps he had engaged in previous murder operations, hence his suspicions. But he indicated no. So my question now is: On this particular day, because we do know that Drago Nikolic apparently was bragging later that he had to show some folks how to kill these innocent Muslims. So I want to know whether this gentleman also killed anyone on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed with your question, Mr. Karnavas, but you have to remember that this is a witness, not an accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour, but his credibility is on the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, did you kill anybody? And please remember that you're under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it's after these events that you go back to the Zvornik Brigade sometime on the morning of the 15th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you try to get home to see your own family members before they set off for the beach for their summer vacation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May I ask: How is it that given your position, your rank, and the conditions and period of the time of war you were able to send your family on a summer vacation to the beach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
