utterances.text: Well, it was not a summer vacation. They went there for health reasons, because my daughter had been in an accident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to talk to you about another subject, and that's with respect to something that was brought up yesterday with respect to your rank and with respect to Mr. Drago Nikolic's rank, if you could help us out. Yesterday you indicated that by 1995 you had the rank of reserve captain, correct, or captain in the reserves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You are not a graduate of the military academy, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But when you were doing your services, your JNA service, back in 1977, as I recall, 1977 and 1978, you were given the opportunity to attend a six-month course in order to become a non-commissioned officer, basically. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you indicated that upon getting out of the JNA service, you held the rank of sergeant but you remained in the reserves all the way from 1978 to 1992, when the war broke out. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when the war started and you became a member of the VRS back in 1992, you held the rank of lieutenant. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course as we indicated, by 1995, three years later, you have been promoted to the rank of captain. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you indicated that Drago Nikolic was a lieutenant. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He was a lieutenant; that's what I said. Okay. Perhaps there was a problem in the translation. You also indicated that he was JNA. It's in the record. That, obviously, was a mistake when you stated it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was an officer because he had graduated from a JNA school. And he worked in the Army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that's the clarification I wanted to make, that he was not with the JNA at the time, but he did, in fact, attend the academy, the JNA academy. And as a result --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. And because -- that academy, as I understand it, is a four- or five-year course, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So when we're trying to make the distinction between a captain and someone who is in the reserves and a lieutenant who is an academy graduate, the captain, such as yourself, and Momir Nikolic would have had only six months of training, versus an officer, an academy graduate, a lieutenant would have five years. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for those reasons, because he was an academy graduate, even though you outranked him, he was able to be your superior officer, if not in rank at least in fact. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you ever in a position, sir, where you were giving orders to superior officers, graduates of the academy, who were colonels, lieutenant colonels, or majors? Were you ever in that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Does it sound logical to you, sir, that a reserve captain with six months of training would be placed in a position where he would be coordinating the activities of and giving orders to officers, academy graduates, who held those ranks of major, lieutenant colonel, colonel, and such?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Depending on your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm saying if a captain in the reserve. Does that make sense to you, given your experience, that a reserve captain would be placed in a position where he was would be giving these sorts of orders to those sorts of ranks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never gave orders. I just made a request for assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to switch to a slightly different topic, and that is with respect to the security organ. From your testimony yesterday, we learned that upon joining the VRS at some point early on you were given the opportunity to attend some classes or schooling which then allowed you to be in the security organ. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that was the training, I believe, that was in Pancevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How many months of training was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't attend this training.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you never had an opportunity to actually go to the training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But nonetheless, because of your interest, I take it, you were able to be a member of the security organ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade, given the size of the brigade, was composed of Drago Nikolic as the chief security officer. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And because this was a regular brigade, the intelligence organ was separate and distinct from the security organ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Later, not at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But now if we're talking 1995, it is distinct and separate. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, the security organ enjoys far more privileges and benefits than the intelligence organ, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, aside from perhaps having your own vehicle strictly designated and dedicated to the security organ, for instance, the security organ could send its reports directly to the security organ of the Drina Corps. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in one part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, that part dealt with what is commonly referred to as counter-intelligence. Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, specific to the Zvornik Brigade, there was some tension between Drago Nikolic and Pandurevic, the commander of the Zvornik Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I never met the man, but I'm told that Mr. Pandurevic was a rather assertive individual. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And not only assertive, but he wanted to be in total and absolute control of his entire brigade, including the security organ. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact as I recall from reading some of your documents, Pandurevic would often remind everyone, including Drago Nikolic, that he, that is, Pandurevic, was the commander. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in trying to control Drago Nikolic, he also tried to ensure that any and all correspondence leaving the Zvornik Brigade would first have to go through Pandurevic before being sent to other -- to the higher echelon. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this was a problem that caused some degree of tension between this lieutenant, who was the head of the security organ, and this -- I believe he was a lieutenant colonel at the time, who was the commander of one of the best-equipped brigades within the Drina Corps. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, in fact, when Pandurevic tried to control Drago Nikolic with respect to the correspondence that he was sending directly to the security organ of the Drina Corps, orders were issued from above that Pandurevic would have to back down, back away, and allow Nikolic, Drago Nikolic, to conduct his affairs as he saw fit. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you were part of that organ; surely you know about the disagreements. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a part of the organ, but I don't have all the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. On that particular night, on the 14th, do you know whether Drago Nikolic contacted Pandurevic to inform him of what he was about to do, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Pandurevic wasn't around the entire time, so I take it Obrenovic was left. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He was in charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. On the 16th of July, did you at any point in time when you were being asked to look for assistance for the killing operation that Popovic was involved, did you contact either Obrenovic or Pandurevic to alarm them of the fact that more innocent Muslim prisoners were about to be executed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, sir, that you and Momir Nikolic were acting in a rather independent manner during those critical days. And when I say "independent," I mean independent from other organs -- I should say Drago Nikolic if that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I corrected myself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Karnavas has got the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm getting the Nikolics mistaken. Both nasty pieces of work, but nonetheless we should be precise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the 14th, on the 14th, Drago Nikolic was engaged with Mr. Popovic, who also is a member of the security organ of the Drina Corps. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at some point you have indicated to the Prosecutor that Nikolic was acting on orders or with the acquiescence of Colonel Beara, who was the head of the security organ of the Main Staff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I said that he had previously had an encounter with Beara, not that he had acted pursuant to orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, do you think for one second, sir, that Beara was not informed of what was going on, given that he had his main assassin - and I use this word in a quite illustrative way - and that is I'm referring to Popovic being out there in the field, directing Nikolic, directing you, directing the military police to kill these innocent prisoners of war. Do you think for one second Beara was not involved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were abreast of what was going on, and they were involved, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you were asked yesterday whether you were able to give orders to Jasikovac, who was the chief of the military police of the Zvornik Brigade, you indicated that, in essence, you were in parity [Realtime transcript read in error "parody"] with him, that you could not order him -- he could not order you, but you could go to Drago Nikolic, should you need Jasikovac's assistance. Am I correct in understanding that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I was able to convey to him what the assignments were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me make sure that I understand this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Karnavas, could you take a look at line 20, this page, because there's a word I don't think is the one you mentioned. And we need to have the correct word.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. Okay. Thank you very, very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, were you on equal footing with Jasikovac. I mean, with Drago Nikolic being at the top of the food chain and then you being an officer and then Jasikovac being the chief of the military police. Do I have it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasikovac was the commander of the military police company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you were to give -- as I understand your previous answer, you could suggest to him what he should do with his military police officers. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was under the chief security officer, mostly. And in his absence, if a request was made to me, then I would convey this request or the order to the commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just so I'm very clear, when Drago Nikolic was absent, were you left then in charge as sort of the acting security officer for the purposes of directing the chief of the military police and how he should use his officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What is part of the job description of my post and in light of the overall authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So as you understand it, that's part of your authority, part of your job description, that when Drago Nikolic isn't there, you have the power, the right, to issue orders to the chief of the military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. If the military -- if the chief of the military police were not around, did you have the power, at least as you understood it to be, to issue orders to the military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't have the power to issue orders, but if they were -- they had the same task as myself, it was either the commander of the military police who would tell them what the task was or would tell them that they would receive instructions from myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: During those days, were they receiving instructions from Popovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. The military police.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, what about on the 14th, was Popovic issuing any orders or did he just -- was sort of the big picture fell on the ground, leaving it up to you and Jasikovac to figure out the details of this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Drago Nikolic who told us this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So Drago Nikolic was on the ground the entire time while this was going on, supervising you and supervising the chief of the military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not present there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may have a moment, Your Honour. I just have a couple of questions left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, one cannot help but notice that as you describe your activities during those days, you show absolutely no remorse or no regrets. Could you please explain to us how do you feel about what you did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't object to the last part of that question, but the first part is a gratuitous. We don't know whether this man has showed regret or not remorse. He's, I guess, making his own personal judgement of his face -- which is not necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The question itself, I have no objection to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I agree with Mr. McCloskey. Maybe you could leave out the first part of the question and just directly come to your questions. We don't know. We really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour, but I must confess I haven't noticed anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As you sit here today, sir, could you please explain to us how do you feel about your conduct and what you did during those days.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I feel remorse and I feel bad about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you believe, sir, that you owe it to the victims and to the surviving members of those families to be indicted and to be sentenced and to be incarcerated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. There's no relevance to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could rephrase this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you believe, sir, that you are guilty of any crimes for which you should be indicted, convicted, and sentenced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With that, Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have five minutes to the break. Mr. Stojanovic, you may begin your cross-examination, or we may have our break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, Your Honour, we would like to use these four minutes to re-organise ourselves. And we would prefer to start after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll resume at 20 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us first go through the part concerning your biography, your personal details.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that's why I would like to ask for private session at this point, Your Honour, in order to protect the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are now in open session. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To speed things up a bit, I will now try to describe the structure of the Zvornik Brigade. It's already been admitted into evidence, the structure, but I just want you to confirm to me that it's right. Do you agree with me that at that time, we're talking about July 1995, the commander of the Zvornik Brigade was Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean throughout July?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about the whole of July of 1995. Was he the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the commander, but he was absent for a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. We know that. But we just want to see what the establishment was like. In July 1995, he was the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, the deputy commander of the brigade and also the chief of staff of the brigade was Dragan Obrenovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Since you already stated that at one point the commander was absent, in that period did his deputy, Dragan Obrenovic, take upon himself all the duties and tasks of the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that on the third level of the chain of command, there were the assistants to the commander, the assistant to the commander for morale, Nenad Simic; assistant for security, Drago Nikolic; and assistant to the commander for logistics, Sretan Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And on the fourth level of the responsibility in the brigade, there were the operations officer -- the operations organ with Mijo Dragutinovic and Milan Maric [phoen] and another officer. I will not go into details in this respect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot give you the chain of command, because I don't know whether they were on the fourth level of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree for the first three levels: The command, his deputy, and the assistants to the commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We will not explore this further. This is quite sufficient. I wanted us to focus on the position of the assistant to the commander for logistics. You told us this was Sretan Milosevic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was his rank in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that he was a captain first class, reserve captain first class.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But according to the establishment, he was on the post which was on the third level in the Zvornik Brigade, in the chain of command of the Zvornik Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I cannot determine what his level in the chain of command was, but I do know what his post, what his duties, were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, a little while ago you said that you could establish the level up to the three levels, the commander, deputy, assistants. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So I can conclude that he was at the third level in terms of importance of his post when we look at the establishment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I believe that you asked some questions which is too specific, which will be very easy to disclose the identity of this witness. Could we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, as an aside, let me just ask you: Is there a duty officer at the forward command post of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is there at the same time a duty officer in the barracks of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us - we're now talking about July 1995 - where the forward command post of the Zvornik Brigade was located.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kitovnice.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name of the place for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kitovnice.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the forward command post linked with the brigade command and the battalion, via communications equipment, telephone or some other kind of equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right in stating that the communications -- the telephone communications from the forward command post, that there was a communication between the forward command post and the battalion, which would bypass the brigade command, that there was a telephone line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wasn't sure whether all the battalions had this kind of lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase that. Do you know whether the first battalion had a direct telephone line with the forward command post, the Pilica Battalion, if we may call it that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And the thing that I'm really interested in: Did the 2nd Battalion have a direct telephone line with the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the schematics, how this was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that certain battalions had direct link with the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Briefly, please, what is the procedure of the handover of duty of the duty officer, and is there a logbook of such handovers of duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is. The procedure is as follows: It is done in the presence of the commander or the commander of the brigade; specific tasks are also related at that time, the tasks relating to that particular shift. The duty officer who is supposed to be relieved must hand over the documentation, together with the minutes, to the person who is supposed to take over the duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So this would have been Ljubo Bojanovic

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who rank did Ljubo Bojanovic have, or what was his duty, according to the establishment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had the rank of major.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could he, without the knowledge of the commander or the chief of staff, assign you to be the duty officer on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had -- previously had any consultations with anyone. But as far as I know, it was said that in the absence of the commander and the chief of staff, then it is the duty operations officer who has authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you personally aware whether Ljubo Bojanovic had consulted the commander or the chief of staff before he told you that you were supposed to take over on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that time the Zvornik Brigade had a battalion which was deployed at Nisici, am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me try to refresh your memory with my following question. Milenko Kajtaz was the battalion commander. Can you now remember that there was a unit that was deployed at the Nisici plateau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not informed about the deployment of the units. I cannot really remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does the name Zoran Janjusic, a member of the military police ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who this person is and how you know him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Janjusic had also come from the area of either Zenica or Kakanj, I'm not sure, and was a member of the Zvornik Brigade with the military police company.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether during that period there were any problems with this particular military police officer and if any proceedings were initiated against him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the reason for these proceedings against this individual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reason being the assistance he had provided in transporting Muslims from one location to another. I cannot remember any specific details.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How did he happen -- how did he help Muslims to move from one place to another, and were those Muslims civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were probably civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- a time frame, otherwise these questions are pretty vague and not very relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. At the beginning of this line of questioning, line 13 and 14, I said: "During this period of time," and I was referring to the first half of 1995. And the witness said: "Yes." But I will try to repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about an event which occurred during the first half of 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot situate this event precisely, but I know that it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that this was in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that would be my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us if this military policeman was ever punished for having helped Muslims to move from one location to another.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He spent some time in detention at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters, but I don't know how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if a criminal report was ever submitted to the military prosecutor because of the assistance he had provided to the enemy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. If that was the case, this would have been done by the chief of legal affairs department and the security --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction, chief of security department. Excuse me, chief of security and legal service.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you involved in the proceedings or in the part of the proceedings against Janjusic, you in your capacity as a security officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, partly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court what your involvement was in this matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic, the security chief, requested that I and an individual from the legal department go to the place of residence, to the house of this individual and carry out a search. After the search was completed, we went back to the headquarters. However, Drago had ordered before that that this individual be detained in the premises of the Zvornik Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally take him to the prison facility at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was this done by the military policemen of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a couple of questions regarding Nesko Djokic and his son. Do you remember this event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court about this event.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure we are talking about the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If there's some relevance to that last line of questioning, the Rules here require that the point be put to the witness. I don't know what the point was otherwise. If they're suggesting there's some wrongdoing or something, the witness needs to have a chance to respond to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, do you take the objections from the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In my subsequent questions, I will ask about relevant aspects of this matter, that is, the participation of the witness in all this. And to show what the attitude of security officer was towards everyone who may have provided assistance to Muslims in this period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I think there should be a relevance to the case in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it would be relevant, and I will stick to the evidence that has been provided by the Prosecutor. I'm not going to go out of this framework, and I will finish this with three or four questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let us see how relevant it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that before -- you said before the intervention of the Prosecutor that you were aware of this event, but then you went on to say that you were not sure we were talking about the same thing. Let me try and be even more specific. Are you aware that proceedings were conducted before the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade against Djokic, father and son, in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were these individuals punished for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What kind of punishment do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they spend any time in detention at the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that for a period of 40 days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how long they were detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was a criminal report submitted to the military prosecutor for the criminal offence of providing assistance to the enemy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. If that was the case, then it must have been Drago Nikolic together with the legal department of the military police who submitted this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you personally involved in this matter and in this investigation, which was conducted by the security department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, partly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of an involvement was it? How were you involved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For me to be able to explain this, I would need much more time. With Your Honours' permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you need a closed session for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't need a closed session. I can just tell you that I was personally at home of these two individuals, the Djokics, while they were in detention, because Drago Nikolic had sent me to their house. He wanted me to be present there, together with the legal department of the military police, who was there to take a statement from the mother, and to bring this statement back to Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions regarding this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just wasn't clear the incident he was referring to. And if he doesn't want to go into it, I won't need to clear it up. But ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The case in question refers to something we have just received from the Prosecutor. This can be seen from the documents that were seized at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters. The documentation includes the criminal report submitted against these individuals. Let me finish this by just one more question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that the Muslims who were involved in this particular case are the individuals who had fled from Branjevo, or rather, from the Branjevo execution site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean in connection with the Djokic family?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just to be clear, the individuals were Muslims who had managed -- who had survived the execution at Branjevo, who had been helped by the Djokics, who were then subject of these proceedings on account of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me now go back to the part of your testimony concerning the night between the 13th and the 14th of July, 1995. You spoke about the arrival of Muslim prisoners on buses and trucks in Orahovac. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, only on buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So there were no trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no trucks where?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That night, were Muslim prisoners brought on trucks as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you remember how many buses arrived on that night bringing Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the precise number, but I know I followed the situation for as long as three buses arrived. After that, I no longer followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that you did not want to follow the situation or could not follow what was going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was no longer paying attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see at one point in time that a vehicle bearing UNPROFOR markings was present there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us please when this procedure of bringing Muslims to Orahovac actually ended. When was it over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometime in the night between the 13th and the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday - let me try to clarify - you said that they had stopped bringing in Muslims sometime during the night, and you have just confirmed this again. But can you tell us exactly when during the night this transport stopped.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you talking about Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The night between the 13th and the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could have been sometime around midnight. I don't know the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So after midnight, no Muslim prisoners were brought to the Orahovac elementary school gym?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 25th and also on the 21st of January, you confirmed that you had been in Orahovac on the 14th and that you had spent the whole day there. Is it correct what you stated yesterday, that during the day, during the 14th of July, no prisoners were brought to the gym in Orahovac, no more prisoners were being brought there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that no more prisoners were brought there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the assistance of the usher, please. If the witness can be shown the transcript which, for the purposes of identification, we marked as D54 and 55. We also have the B/C/S translation of the transcript. This is the testimony of witnesses Kemal Mehmedovic and Mevludin Oric. Could the witness be shown the B/C/S version so that he could follow. Your Honour, I'm referring to the transcript from the testimony of Kemal Mehmedovic, who was heard before this Tribunal. It was a session held on the 15th of July. For identification, it was page 1277, line 13 through 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like us to go through this together. So Witness Kemal Mehmedovic, a survivor of the execution in Orahovac, testified before this Tribunal. And he stated the following. The question of the Prosecutor was: "So what time did your vehicle finally leave the area roughly," meaning Bratunac, where they had spent the night between the 13th and the 14th. The witness responds: "Do you mean on the way out of Bratunac or in front of the garages?" Prosecutor: "On the way out of Bratunac." The witness answers: "Well, we left possibly sometime between 10.00 and 12.00 because I think we arrived down there maybe in the early afternoon. And we only stopped very briefly on the way. There was a lot of -- many hours were spent standing, but I don't know how many because I didn't have a watch." "And what direction did your vehicle go in?" "In the direction of Konjevic, Polje and Zvornik." Were you able to follow this testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So this witness states that he spent the night between the 13th and the 14th in Bratunac. And when asked by the Prosecutor, he answers that on the 14th in the morning, sometime between 10.00 and 12.00, he set off in this column towards Orahovac, and that they arrived there in the early afternoon. You have this page in front of you, that would be page 1277, lines 13 through 18. When asked by us you answered, while under oath, that nobody else was brought in after midnight in the night of the 13th to the 14th of July, 1995. You stated, furthermore - again, you are under oath - on the 21st of January and on the 25th of January, you stated to the Prosecutor that you had spent the entire day there. You had undertaken to speak the truth. You said that nobody had been brought in, nobody else. A survivor of this event, Kemal Mehmedovic, states that it was in the early afternoon and that he had set off from Bratunac between 10.00 and 12.00. So who is not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I said that as far as I could remember, the transportation of Muslims by bus was organised, that they were transported from Srebrenica to Orahovac, and that the transportation was completed during the night. Now, as to whether there were any individual arrivals, I don't know about that and I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, Kemal Mehmedovic, in a very moving testimony, spoke about this long column moving from Bratunac to Orahovac. He spoke about the size of the column. He spoke about how the column was escorted, how it was organised, and how they had to wait and gather in front of the Vihor garage for the column to be formed, the column that would then go on to Orahovac. Yet, today you tell us that after midnight, there were no organised arrivals. But you do not rule out the possibility that there may have been individual arrivals. This witness speaks about organised arrivals in the afternoon of the 14th of July. Is he then not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Upon receiving the task in the Zvornik Brigade relating to the reception and the accommodation of the Muslims from Srebrenica in the gym of the Orahovac elementary school, I did not have any other insight or any other knowledge pertaining to the organised arrivals of columns of vehicles, except for the fact that Drago Nikolic on that night when he came to Orahovac - I can't be specific about the time - told me that there were other buses with people from Srebrenica arriving and leaving to Petkovci, Rocevic, and Pilica, for the people to be accommodated there. But I was not the only person there in Orahovac. Jasikovac was also there, and if perhaps this vehicle came and was taken in in his presence, it doesn't necessarily mean that I would have to know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I know that you testified to this effect, but something doesn't fit in here. Is it possible that in the afternoon of the 14th, a column of vehicles appeared escorted by UNPROFOR vehicles, and the people on the vehicles were then taken off the buses and put in the gym without you knowing about it at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The only conclusion I can draw then is that it is possible that Witness Kemal Mehmedovic wasn't telling the truth. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's argumentative and not relevant for this person to make that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I think the Bench will draw the conclusion from the serious questions you asked. You may move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will now ask the witness to have a look at the next exhibit, which would be D63 for identification purposes. This is a transcript of the testimony of Mevludin Oric, a survivor of the Orahovac event. He testified before this Tribunal on the 21st of July, 2003. The page is 1349, lines 6 through 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So again, this is a witness who is a survivor of the events in Orahovac who testified before this Tribunal. And when asked by the Prosecutor what happened next morning, that is the question, he answers: "The next morning, that was the 14th, the morning of the 14th, they told us that they were taking us to Kladanj to be exchanged as prisoners of war." The Prosecutor then asks: "So what did you see?" The witness answers: "We waited there for a while, for this column to start. We were told that we had to wait. When we left Bratunac, we parked at the Vihor parking lot. We waited there, and we were told that we had to wait for UNPROFOR because they were due to arrive from Potocari." And so on. Sir, what is the distance between Bratunac and Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact distance, 50, 60 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If it is a column of vehicles which is driving at a slow rate of speed, relatively speaking, a column that has its escort, it's a column that consists of buses and trucks, what would you say? How long would it take for this column to arrive from Bratunac to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot give you an estimate as to their speed and the time that it would take them to arrive there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But at any rate, they would need at least a few hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to the testimony of this witness, he also confirms that the column, which again consisted of five buses, four trucks, and an UNPROFOR vehicle, did on that day in the afternoon of the 14th arrive to Orahovac. Can you remember, if you were indeed present there, whether this column had arrived in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there. I don't remember that the column arrived in front of the gym in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this witness testified about being in the gym. He testified about the events in the gym, about how he was taken out of the gym, loaded on to a truck, and taken or driven to the execution site. He was in the gym; that's his testimony. He was there on the 14th, that's when he was brought in, in the afternoon of the 14th. Is it possible -- would it be possible for you not to see this column that was so large?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already told you, I was present there. I don't remember about the arrival of this column in front of the gym in the Orahovac elementary school. I cannot state that this column -- that it was impossible for this column to be anywhere else in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps this would be a good moment, Your Honour, to adjourn, since I will continue with another line of questioning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, could you please tell me how long your cross-examination will last.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask you for the time that you are prepared to allot to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, just give me an indication, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that we should be finished in one, one and a half, maybe two sessions, but I really don't want to interfere with your schedule. I would then have the opportunity to cut down my questions tonight or perhaps even expand the number of questions, if you allow me to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I understand that this week we still have two witnesses waiting on the list. Of course I want you to streamline your questions for tomorrow's session and try to finish this witness as soon as possible. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness that's next is here and should be ready to go tomorrow and Thursday. And the way it's looking and in my discussions, I think we're going to have plenty of time for that witness. The other witness, Kate Barr, the handwriting person, should be ready to testify on Friday, and one day for a handwriting expert should be plenty of time. So it looks like we're on schedule and shouldn't have a problem and then the next few [sic]. I do have a new bit of information that the investigation has learned that I wanted to alert the Court of. I don't know if now is the time. I can alert you tomorrow morning. I just found out about it today, the possibility of another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think it's proper for us to discuss about this specific witness before this witness. Maybe you could discuss it tomorrow. Well, I think we'll resume tomorrow afternoon in the same courtroom, and the -- well, the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
